headline: In May 2026, Southborough approved comprehensive permit conditions for a 32-unit 40B development, awarded the Neary School feasibility design contract, and backed regional dispatch borrowing.
synopsis: Land use decisions moved forward as the Zoning Board of Appeals approved comprehensive permit conditions for a 32-unit Chapter 40B development at 250 Turnpike Road, while the Planning Board adopted new native plant landscaping rules and recommended revoking occupancy for 40-42 Central Street. School facility planning advanced as the Select Board awarded the Neary Elementary School feasibility study design contract to Tappe Architects, while engineering assessments highlighted immediate roof failure at Neary. Both the local and regional school committees renewed food service contracts with Whitsons Culinary Group, though the regional renewal required reconsideration after an initial failure over meal quality concerns. The Select Board approved up to $12.5 million in temporary bridge borrowing for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center and elected new board leadership. Southborough also joined Westborough in endorsing a $150,000 state grant application to study infrastructure, zoning, and wastewater along the Route 9 and Interstate 495 corridor.

top_items.title: ZBA approves 250 Turnpike Road 40B permit conditions
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to approve comprehensive permit conditions for a 32-unit Chapter 40B rental townhouse development.
top_items.body: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved the draft comprehensive permit decision, findings, and conditions for the proposed 32-unit rental development at 250 Turnpike Road and 9 Parkerville Road. Eight of the units (25 percent) will be deed-restricted as affordable for households earning up to 80 percent of area median income. The approved decision outlines dozens of requirements for the applicant, including engineering peer oversight, stormwater controls, mitigation in the wetland buffer zone, and accommodations for site traffic and school bus pickup. Vertical construction cannot begin until remaining state and local wastewater and environmental approvals are secured.

top_items.title: Architect selected for Neary School feasibility study
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to award the Neary Elementary School feasibility study design contract to Tappe Architects.
top_items.body: Acting on a recommendation from the Elementary School Building Committee, the Select Board voted to award the Neary School feasibility study contract to Tappe Architects and authorized contract negotiations. Tappe was selected from five submitted proposals and three interviewed finalists based on community engagement planning and school design experience. Separately, engineering consultants from SOCOTEC informed the School Committee that Neary's 30-year-old roof is in active failure with roughly 8,000 linear feet of failed seams and detached insulation, prompting immediate short-term stabilization plans while capital replacement options are prepared.

top_items.title: Select Board approves $12.5 million regional dispatch borrowing
top_items.why: The Select Board authorized up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing to bridge state grant funding for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center.
top_items.body: In a 4-1 vote, the Select Board approved up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing authority to bridge state grant funding for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center. The short-term borrowing ensures regional construction contracts can proceed without delays between state 911 development grant disbursements, aligning Southborough with partner towns Grafton and Westborough. Dissent on the board centered on whether Southborough should assume borrowing risk on behalf of the regional district.

top_items.title: Planning Board adopts townwide Native Landscape Regulations
top_items.why: The Planning Board voted unanimously to require 100 percent native vegetation in site plan review projects and ban neonicotinoid pesticides.
top_items.body: The Planning Board held a public hearing and voted 5-0 to adopt new Native Landscape Regulations for projects undergoing site plan review, developed in collaboration with the Open Space Preservation Commission. The regulations require 100 percent of newly planted vegetation to consist of native New England species, prohibit the use of systemic neonicotinoid pesticides, and restrict dyed mulches and invasive species. The rules are intended to enhance local ecological health and pollinator habitat, while broader rules governing off-site invasive species were deferred for future study.

top_items.title: Whitsons food service contracts renewed after regional revote
top_items.why: Both school committees voted to renew food service contracts with Whitsons Culinary Group for the 2026-2027 school year.
top_items.body: The Southborough School Committee and the Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee both approved one-year contract renewals for Whitsons Culinary Group with a 3.9 percent fee increase tied to the Consumer Price Index. At the regional level, an initial renewal motion failed 3-4-2 following committee discussions regarding meal quality, food options, and staff morale. The Regional School Committee reconsidered and voted 8-1 to approve the contract after being advised that non-renewal would leave the high school without food service vendor options for the start of the school year.

top_items.title: Planning Board recommends revoking occupancy for 40-42 Central Street
top_items.why: The Planning Board voted 4-1 to recommend that the Building Commissioner revoke the temporary certificate of occupancy for 40-42 Central Street.
top_items.body: The Planning Board reviewed outstanding non-compliance issues regarding the Southborough Historical Society's property at 40-42 Central Street and voted 4-1 to recommend that the Building Commissioner revoke its temporary certificate of occupancy. Members cited unfulfilled site conditions, including unresolved accessible parking corrections, lack of parking lot lighting reviews, and unpaid peer review fees. The board also forwarded a briefing package to Town Counsel to explore formal enforcement options.

top_items.title: Town boards endorse joint Route 9 and I-495 corridor study
top_items.why: Southborough boards backed a joint application with Westborough for a $150,000 state grant to study commercial corridor zoning, infrastructure, and wastewater.
top_items.body: The Planning Board and Wastewater Study Committee voted to support a joint application with the Town of Westborough for a $150,000 Massachusetts One Stop for Growth grant. The study would evaluate zoning, commercial economic development opportunities, and infrastructure along the Route 9 and Interstate 495 corridor. The project requires a $7,500 local match from each municipality, with Southborough officials emphasizing the goal of identifying commercial wastewater options to broaden the town's commercial tax base.
